chunks.rationale: electron/orchServer.js is the whole fix. Read assertUserApproved first (the new gate), then its one call site inside thread_merge — the gate fires ONLY when the lead has no worktree of its own, because that is the case where mergeWorktree commits to the project's default branch. A lead that has a worktree keeps merging workers onto its own branch unasked; that is staging, and the user still gates the lead's branch from the thread header. requireLandableWorker is a pure extraction of thread_merge's old preflight so thread_pr shares it — diff it against the old body and check nothing was dropped. thread_pr is new and delegates to the existing createPr; it deliberately does NOT clean up the worker's worktree.
risks: approved:true is the agent's own claim. The real lock is the turn check; if isAutoTurn is missing from a runner (test fakes, any future createToolHandlers caller) the gate falls open to the claim alone.

A lead that forks a worker and polls it to done inside its own human turn can still merge without asking — the turn genuinely is human-started, just not an answer to a question. The notice path (the common case, and the one that put 13 branches on main) is covered.

requireLandableWorker throws for a missing worker worktree nowhere — thread_merge still returns merged:false for a worktree:false worker, thread_pr throws. Confirm the two callers handle that case differently on purpose.

chunks.rationale: electron/runner.js has two small changes. isAutoTurn exposes the existing autoTurns map (already the codebase's own definition of 'human in the loop', see the comment at startRun) — no new state. The worker-finished notice text is the behavioural half: it used to say 'call thread_merge', which is what the lead obeyed. It now says report and ask. Verify the notice and the tool description agree, since the agent reads both.
risks: autoTurns resets to 0 on any startRun without fromNotice, which includes machine-ish paths (verify auto-fix). Those would read as human turns; merge still needs approved:true so the blast radius is one gate, not both.
Instruction/notice wording is the only thing steering a lead that has NOT yet hit the gate. If the wording and the refusal text disagree the agent will loop.

chunks.rationale: orch-merge.test.js replaces the old 'merges into the project checkout when the lead has no worktree' case — that test asserted exactly the behaviour being removed, so read the replacement pair (refuses / approved) together. The isAutoTurn case builds its own handlers with a fake that returns true. thread_pr coverage is gate-and-guards only: the push/gh half belongs to createPr and would need a CODER_GH_BIN fake (POSIX-only, per the fakeBin split).
risks: thread_pr's happy path is untested here — a typo in the createPr argument shape would not be caught by this suite.
Behaviour change for crews already running: their next worker-finished notice will refuse the merge they were told to do. Intended, but it will look like a regression to an in-flight orchestration.

Full electron suite run green (1682 pass) after building core/dist; a second run showed the known flaky 'wireClient x webBridge over a real socket'. Renderer suite not run — no renderer files changed.
